purpose: Fosamprenavir is used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children. It is always used together with other HIV medicines as part of a combination treatment plan. It helps lower the amount of HIV in your body and keeps your immune system stronger.
how_it_works: HIV needs a special tool called a protease enzyme to make copies of itself inside your body. Fosamprenavir blocks that tool, so the virus cannot finish making new copies of itself. This slows down the spread of HIV in your body and helps protect your immune system from further damage.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache, tiredness, and skin rash. Some people may notice a mild to moderate rash, especially in the first few weeks of treatment. Tell your doctor if a rash develops, especially if it is severe or comes with fever.
warnings: Fosamprenavir can cause a serious or life-threatening skin rash in rare cases — seek medical help right away if you get a severe rash, blistering, or mouth sores. It can raise your cholesterol and blood sugar levels, so your doctor will monitor these. It interacts with many other medications, including some common drugs, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything you take. Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to amprenavir. If you have a sulfa drug allergy, let your doctor know, as there may be a related risk.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is either 1400 mg twice daily without a booster, or 700 mg twice daily combined with ritonavir 100 mg twice daily (ritonavir helps your body absorb more of the medicine). It can be taken with or without food. Your doctor will decide the best dose for you based on your specific situation and other medicines you take.
